region.name: Direct Report 1on1s
region.summary: Manager 1on1 notes and private reads on direct reports Lin, Kavi, Nadia, and Renee, covering design and growth decisions, the investing GA go/no-go, hiring and comp exceptions, retention risk, and follow-up commitments.

brief.text:
This region holds the manager's weekly 1on1 notes and private reads on four direct reports: Lin (sole designer), Kavi (Growth/experimentation), Nadia Okafor (iOS/mobile lead and hiring manager), and Renee (driving the investing GA launch). With Lin, the manager approved a 3-month contract designer for routine UI work. Web stays lower priority than mobile, and the design system will not be formalized until there are 2+ designers. Lin stays on the IC track while mentoring the contractor. In the investing tab mock review, the performance-vs-portfolio-value question was closed in favor of leading with performance, auto-invest setup was cut from 8 to 5 screens, and a quarterly internal design audit was agreed. The manager also told Lin unprompted that she is underpaid and committed to an adjustment after the Series B. With Kavi, topics included A/B testing push vs. email vs. both, a standing weekly Plaid bank-linking data drop, and 24h-stale Snowflake features. Those features get fixed within a quarter by ADR-030, which moves ML features to Postgres. Round-up sweep ownership was split: Payments owns the job and Growth owns the multiplier config.

Retention and comp threads run throughout. Kavi is frustrated by the experiment freeze. The manager asked him to raise it in eng staff rather than in Slack DMs, and reads him as frustrated but not a flight risk for now. Kavi pre-registers the first three post-GA experiments and has already delivered round-up results. The manager owes Kavi an unfreeze date and a yes/no on copy-only tests. Private notes on Nadia say she is quietly checking market salaries for senior iOS and EM roles, so her comp trajectory should be made explicit before the next cycle. She is described as steady, trusted, and high-potential, and a post-Series B comp conversation is pending. In the 2026-10-06 1on1, Nadia reported a unanimous panel yes for Ama as senior iOS. The senior iOS band is below market and Ama's current comp sits at the top of it, so Nadia requested a comp exception backed by a 55% offer-accept rate. This is tracked as an open risk ('Senior iOS offer tight on comp', severity 27, owner Nadia), alongside 'Losing Ama and restarting search' (severity 4). Nadia also reported that Theo is progressing well and that she liked Grace as a VP Eng candidate, though she is an interested party. Her other 1on1 items covered the mobile-side response to the April incident, her capacity, and Q3 planning ownership.

Renee's thread covers the investing GA go/no-go. Go/no-go #1 surfaced three blockers: the reconciliation fix, the disclosure review, and Android parity. The GA target remains Oct 20, with go/no-go #2 on Oct 16. The card soft launch moved to Q1 2027 to protect investing GA and the Series B, and Kavi's freeze needs a firm date. The reconciliation fix is logged as the main GA risk (severity 4, owner Devon). Related open compliance items are the todo 'Complete Q3 access review' (severity 28, owner Sam) and the risk that a missed Q3 access review becomes a SOC 2 Type II exception (owner Sam Whitfield). This region can answer questions such as what was decided in a given person's 1on1, who is a retention risk, the status of the Ama offer and comp exception, what the manager owes each report, why card launch slipped, and what is blocking investing GA.

items.title: Summarize my recent 1:1s with Nadia. What does she need from me?
items.body:
## Recent 1:1s with Nadia Okafor

Your map has three logged 1:1s, with the two most recent carrying the live threads [c14].

**2026-09-15 (60 min).** She opened on comp before you'd even sat down — "calm, prepared, clearly rehearsed," with market research she'd done back in May. She's been a TL *and* a manager since Aug 18 but is paid as a TL, and asked whether the manager trial comes with a comp review and when. You told her yes, after the Series B closes (target mid-November), in the first cycle after. She accepted it, then noted evenly that this was the **second** time she'd heard "post-Series B" from you — which your own notes confirm was in the May 1:1. Your read: "If I miss this, I lose more than money with her." Also covered: Theo four weeks in and shipping his first investing-tab fix; that managing is "less about technical guidance, more about noticing," and the hardest part is not fixing his PRs herself; and an early flag that the Ama offer would be tight on comp. You brought her the fractional-share mismatch (0.4% of positions off after a corporate action) — not her bug, but her screen [c26].

**2026-10-06 (45 min).** The panel came back a unanimous yes on **Ama** for senior iOS — strong on SwiftUI/TCA, has run a refactor like yours at a larger app, and Nadia sees her anchoring the second half of the iOS rewrite. The blocker is comp: your senior iOS band is below market and Ama's current comp already sits at the top of it, so a lateral won't land her. Nadia argued with data, not adjectives — 55% offer-accept rate, declines concentrated in senior mobile: *"The band is the reason, not the pitch."* You raised comp yourself this time so she wouldn't have to ask a third time; she said "I know," then "I'll believe it when it's on paper." Theo is going well enough that she's letting him run his own standups. She was on Grace Liu's panel that morning and liked how Grace talks about growing first-time managers — noted as an interested party, since she'd report to the VP Eng [c20].

Your read: two months in, she's clearly good at managing. **The trial is over in everything but paperwork** [c20] [c14].

## What she needs from you

Her profile states it in four points [c14]:

1. **The comp review, on paper, in the first cycle after close.** No third "post-close."
2. **A decision on Ama's comp exception this week** — plus a real fix to the senior iOS band in the 2027 budget, not a one-off exception.
3. **Formalizing the manager track**, so she isn't doing two jobs on one title.
4. **Room.** She doesn't need managing on iOS architecture.

### Open commitments — yours

| Owner | Item | Due | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **You** | Raise the senior iOS band with Jordan for the 2027 budget | 2026-10-23 | Open [c20] |
| **You** | Comp review for Nadia, first cycle after close | 2026-11-30 | Open [c20] [c26] |
| **You** | Formalize the manager track at that same review | — | Open [c26] |
| Nadia | Get Ama's offer through comp approval | 2026-10-10 | Open — **now past due** [c21] [c23] |

⚠️ **The Ama offer is the time-critical item and it's slipped.** As of Oct 8, Maya approved the $245k offer from the engineering side, but **Jordan's budget sign-off (due Oct 9) and Aleks' above-band comp approval (due Oct 10) were both still outstanding**, as were Priya N.'s reference checks (2 of 3 done, due Oct 12) [c24]. The named risk is losing Ama and restarting a three-month search for the role your post-close plan depends on [c20] [c1]. The approval is assigned to Nadia to chase, but the unblocking signatures aren't hers.

### Two things she owes that may need your air cover
- **Theo's 60-day written feedback**, due 2026-10-16 — still unchecked [c27].
- **Android parity on 2 investing screens**, merged behind a feature flag, due **Oct 15** — one day before go/no-go #2 on Oct 16, with GA targeted Oct 20 and at risk. Scoping is done; open items are the flag-gated merge, design QA with Lin, disclosure verification, and Play Store submission [c15]. She's also one of the system owners with a pending Q3 access review signature [c15].

**The pattern worth naming:** the comp promise, the band fix, and the manager-track paperwork all resolve at the same post-close review — and that review is now carrying two deferrals' worth of trust. Your own note frames the risk precisely: she's patient, and you keep spending that patience [c26].

*Note on sourcing: the structured risk/todo items ([c1], [c15], [c21], [c23], [c27]) are derived signals extracted from the underlying notes rather than verbatim 1:1 text, so dates and owners there are inferred from checklist lines. The May 19 1:1 is referenced in both later notes but I didn't retrieve its full contents.*
